# Stage 2 report: RAG with citations and evals

This report is in progress. Its sections are filled in as the stage 2 pipeline is built, and every number will come from a script in this repo.

The stage 1 report (structured extraction) is in [docs/reports/stage-1.md](docs/reports/stage-1.md).

## Retrieval metrics
<!-- retrieval:start (generated by `make eval-retrieval`; edits here are overwritten) -->

15 questions from `evals/retrieval_gold.toml`, no filters, top 10 chunks per search. Embedding model `google/embeddinggemma-300m`, reranker `BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3-int8`. Settings from config.toml, none tuned on these questions: 50 candidates per retriever, RRF k 60, BM25 k1 1.2 and b 0.75, 30 hybrid candidates reranked. A chunk is a hit when it comes from the evidence document and contains its quote; rules in docs/METRICS.md. One question is 1/15 of a recall value.

Default-setup rule (fixed before the run): on the `structure` collection, the highest MRR@10, then the higher recall@5, then the setup without a reranker. Result: **hybrid+rerank** (MRR@10 0.615). This choice is made on the gold set itself; no numeric setting was tuned on it.

Best on `fixed` by the same rule: hybrid+rerank (MRR@10 0.703), above the `structure` choice.

**Gold set (S2-09).** `evals/retrieval_gold.toml` holds 15 questions (en 6, uk 4, de 3, fr 1, it 1) over PDF, HTML, DOCX and Markdown documents. Each question names its evidence: document, section, page (PDF only) and a short exact quote (decision 16). A retrieved chunk counts as correct when it comes from the evidence document and contains the quote, with whitespace ignored. All 15 questions were drafted by Claude at the user's request (the user does not read German, French or Italian well) and reviewed by the user. `make retrieval-gold-check` confirms that every quote is in its document, on its page, and whole inside at least one chunk of both chunking strategies.

**How it is measured (S2-10).** `make eval-retrieval` runs each setup on both chunking strategies and scores the returned chunks with the gold-set hit rule; `docs/METRICS.md` defines recall@k and MRR. The table above is generated from `evals/results/retrieval.json`, and two runs give the same ranks. The search settings were committed in S2-07 and S2-08, before the gold set existed, and none was changed for this measurement. The one decision taken on these 15 questions is the default search setup, by the rule stated above: `make search` now reranks by default. The answer pipeline keeps the structure-aware chunks although fixed-size chunks score higher here: a fixed-size chunk is labelled with the section where it starts, and the answer usually sits in a later section, so a citation would name the wrong section.

**Section labels (S2-12).** `make section-labels` checks this without models. Every chunk that holds a gold quote carries the right section label for 15 of 15 questions with structure-aware chunks, against 4 of 15 with fixed-size chunks. Over the whole corpus, 6968 of 16236 (chunk, block) pairs of fixed-size chunks have the right label (42.9 %), against all 13015 for structure-aware chunks, which are right by construction. Rules in `docs/METRICS.md`, per-question detail in [evals/results/section_labels.md](evals/results/section_labels.md), and the full chunking rationale in the README.
